items.headline: Claude Code just broke the world record for world's largest known reversible prime number (aka emirp) with one day of CPU time. 10069 digits long
items.summary: An emirp is a prime number which is also prime when the decimal digits are reversed (eg 13 and 31, or 10069 and 96001). Numberphile posted this video last week about a newly found world record emirp, which used arithmetic hacks and drew on extensive effort and knowledge from prime finding communities.
